text.p: These are the leading stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- S E R B I A -
NASA BORBA

- U.S. Congress posed three special conditions for the normalisation of relations with Serbia -- to ensure free and fair presidental and parliamentary elections in 1997, honour their results and build democratic institutions including strenghtening of independent media and respect of the law.
- Belgrade university students marched in the streets protesting over proposed hikes in school fees, demanded resignation of government over difficult social situation.
- Medics' strike continues despite the Serbian government regulation instructing them to ensure the minimum of work.
- International federation of newspaper publishers said unjust imposition of taxes on independent media was a direct attack on the freedom of the press in a letter to the Serbian prime minister.
- Serbian Renewal Movement (SPO), one of the Zajedno coalition partners, says it is ready to participate alone at forthcoming elections.
- Money supply M1 in Yugoslavia increased by 320 million dinars in May to reach 5.881 billion dinars, says Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce banking committee.

- Eight Serbian invalids of the last war go on a hunger strike, in a second protest since March, demanding unpaid benefits and right to free medical treatment. A protest rally planned for June 26 if their demands are not met.
- Federal government proposed new customs duties to be in force from August 1.
POLITIKA
- Serbian Development Fund determined criteria for allocating credits to firms with profitable export programmes.
- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic received Belgian Defence Minister Jean-Paul Poncelet. Both sides stressed the important role of international forces in Eastern Slavonia in Croatia.
- Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic received Iraqi trade minister Mohamid Mahid Saleh stressed Yugoslavia's interest in renewing cooperation with Iraq.
- Yugoslav and Macedonian delegations are discussing border demarcation and social insurance accords in Skopje.
- Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic said Serbia would pass the ownership transformation law which was the real way to market economy.

- Talks with international financial institutions started a month ago will continue at the end of this week or early next week, said Yugoslav minister for cooperation with international financial organisations Nebojsa Maljkovic.
- The state will secure a credit line to the agricultural sector which will enable food exports worth $750 million this year, says Serbian Agriculture Minister Jovan Babovic.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Yugoslav government proposes amendments to the tax law; sales tax to be 10 percent for products affecting the living standard and 20 percent for other products.
BORBA
- Serbia plans to invest $2.6 billion in power industry and $1.2 billion in oil industry by the year 2000, says vice president of the Serbian Chamber of Commerce Momir Pavlicevic.
- Yugoslav bank card (YUBA), a project of the Yugoslav Banking Association, expected to be issued in early summer.
BLIC

- Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic says ministers of health, education and social protection are not to blame for empty funds from these sectors causing difficulties in payment of wages and resulting strikes.
- M O N T E N E G R O -
POBJEDA
- Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic, Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic and Parliament Speaker Svetozar Marovic separately recieved U.S. charge d'affaires in Belgrade Richard Miles.

- Bulatovic, Djukanovic and Marovic took part in discussions of the Ulcinj branch of the Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS). Despite obvious disagreements between top officials all of them are opposed to proposed changes of the federal constitution.

- President Momir Bulatovic and Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic were invited to address republic's parliament on Wednesday. Djukanovic is expected to respond to president Bulatovic's accusations of criminal activity.
- DPS local branch of Budva asks responsibility of president Bulatovic for endangering party unity.
- Montenegrin Deputy Prime Minister Slavko Drljevic submitted his resignation.
- Average net salary in Montenegro in May stood at 797 dinars, the republican statistics office said. -- Belgrade newsroom + 381 11 222 4305
